topics.title: USDI on CKB will be discontinued. Any alternative for stablecoin?

recent_posts.topic_title: USDI on CKB will be discontinued. Any alternative for stablecoin?
recent_posts.author: ckbbkc
recent_posts.content_text: No one has mentioned demand. Where does the demand for stablecoins on CKB come from? What is the user activity level on CKB? How many users does CKB have? So, is it true that stablecoins alone cannot achieve scale?

recent_posts.topic_title: USDI on CKB will be discontinued. Any alternative for stablecoin?
recent_posts.author: ckbbkc
recent_posts.content_text: If CKB has a large user base, the difference between using a bridged stablecoin and a native stablecoin is merely a matter of user experience, not a matter of whether there is a demand for it.
recent_posts.content_html: If CKB has a large user base, the difference between using a bridged stablecoin and a native stablecoin is merely a matter of user experience, not a matter of whether there is a demand for it.

recent_posts.topic_title: USDI on CKB will be discontinued. Any alternative for stablecoin?
recent_posts.author: ckbbkc
recent_posts.content_text: To this day, CKB has never considered how to attract players (infrastructure needs to be used on a large scale to be considered infrastructure). Demand drives developers to create, or rather, developers create applications that truly attract users. Essentially, it’s a cycle: attracting developers and attracting players are the two ends that drive this cycle forward.
